speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what is the current per capita cost of running Day Activity Centre services for adults with disabilities with moderate to high needs; and (b) what is the current per capita grant provided by the Government for such Day Activity Centre services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Besides funding from the Government, DACs also receive funding from the community, such as through Tote Board and their own fund-raising.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: A lot of the charities that are running services for the moderate to high needs individuals with disabilities are facing a lot of challenges on the ground, based on this current funding model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) has been trying to help, but the challenges remain.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And then, to identify what are some alternate and more innovative financing models for DACs for disabled adults with moderate to high support needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Debating at a very general level and asking Parliamentary Questions (PQs) and replying to PQs at this level is not going to solve matters.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The reason is that the costs are indeed high.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are also issues like fee cap and you cannot charge that much sometimes.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: They will then keep their children at home and that is not always the best quality of life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is what, I think, Minister Vivian Balakrishnan, when he was MSF Minister actually looked at.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, there are some models that can be considered.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: If we do not solve this problem, then, cohorts of graduates from the special schools with mid to high needs are really going to suffer.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I hope the Ministry will look into this deeply with those of us who really want to solve this issue.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I share that passion as well in doing more for the community, especially for those with moderate to severe needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I totally agree with her that staying at home, not consuming any of these services, is not going to be the way to go.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That helped about half of the community with some of the fees.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will be launching that by the second half of this year.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will provide learning, social activities as well as respite care at locations that are closer to where persons with disabilities, including those with moderate needs, as well as their caregivers, live.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We take the Member's points on board and we look forward to that continued engagement and exploration with the community and the Member herself to see what better we can do for the community.
